definitions.explanation: A dog without an owner that wanders freely. Can also be used figuratively to describe a person who belongs to no group or organization.

examples.japanese: {野良犬|のらいぬ}に{近|ちか}づくな。
{公園|こうえん}で{野良犬|のらいぬ}を{見|み}かけて{保健所|ほけんじょ}に{連絡|れんらく}した。
examples.english: I spotted a stray dog in the park and contacted the public health center.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}は{野良犬|のらいぬ}がたくさんいたが、{今|いま}ではほとんど{見|み}かけなくなった。
examples.english: There used to be many stray dogs, but nowadays you hardly ever see them.

notes:
USAGE:
{野良|のら} means "stray" or "feral" and combines with animal names: {野良犬|のらいぬ} (stray dog), {野良猫|のらねこ} (stray cat). {野良|のら} alone originally means "field" or "open land" and also appears in {野良仕事|のらしごと} (farm work).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {野良犬|のらいぬ}を{保護|ほご}する (to rescue a stray dog)
- {野良犬|のらいぬ}に{噛|か}まれる (to be bitten by a stray dog)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Stray dogs have become rare in modern Japan due to strict animal control laws and active efforts by {保健所|ほけんじょ} (public health centers). In contrast, {野良猫|のらねこ} (stray cats) are still commonly seen.
